newsitem.title: USA: Stocks edge higher in lackluster trading.
newsitem.headline: Stocks edge higher in lackluster trading.

text.p: Stocks rose Wednesday, though the market showed signs of weariness after its recent record-setting rally.

Just after 1:10 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 29.07 points at 7,568.34, above Tuesday's record of 7,539.27. Gainers edged losers by a 13-10 margin on the New York Stock Exchange, where volume was a moderate 299 million shares.
But the Nasdaq composite index fell again as high-technology stocks continued to come under pressure. The Nasdaq lost 5.34 points to 1,396.35.
Investors were pausing for breath, some were taking profits and many were awaiting fresh reports on the economy, analysts said.

"We've had a market that has soared in a vacuum of economic news," said Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management. "The market's fingerprints suggest it wants to go higher until something tells it to stop."
Analysts said the May retail sales data, due Thursday, and the Producer Price Index due Friday may temper the four-day rally that brought the Dow past 7,500 this week for the first time.
Charles Payne of Wall Street Strategies said the market was consolidating and taking stock after a remarkable run.

"I think there are a lot of people, especially the old-timers, who are getting concerned," he said, adding that a correction in the market is almost inevitable, though the timing and size are unknown.
"Eventually it is going to happen, but for right now we're sort of moving along nicely," Payne said.
But others said the rally could continue.
"Barring any unforeseen things, the market has room to rally," said Gail Dudack, chief investment strategist at UBS Securities.

Investors have been ploughing funds into stocks ahead of upcoming second-quarter earnings reports and next month's meeting of Federal Reserve policy-makers, who will weigh their next move on interest rates.
The central bank raised rates in March in a bid to slow the economy and ward off inflation, the first increase in more than two years. But the policy-makers held short-term rates steady last month.
The American Stock Exchange index added 0.99 of a point to 622.10.
